page:
Environment API for Vite: formalizing client and server environments. Vite 6 introduces formal environments concept. Backward compatible with Vite 5.
- Formalizes environments: client, ssr (optional)
- Until Vite 5: two implicit environments (client, optional ssr)
- New API: create multiple custom environments
- Backward compatibility: Vite 5 config works seamlessly in Vite 6
- Simple SPA/MPA: no new APIs exposed (client environment applied internally)
- SSR apps: two environments (client: browser, ssr: Node/server runtime)
- Dev server execution: server code runs in Node process (close to production)
- Alternative runtimes: Cloudflare workerd, edge servers
- Vite 6: configure app to map all production environments
- Single dev server: run code in multiple environments concurrently
- Source code transformed by Vite dev server
- HTTP server, middlewares, resolved config, plugins shared
- Independent dev environments per configuration
- Each env matched to production environment
- Module runner: fetches and evaluates transformed code
- Environments configuration: build.sourcemap, optimizeDeps, server/edge specific options
- build option: recursive config inheritance (child inherits parent)
- top-level options apply to client environment
- optimizeDeps: client environment only (doesn't work well for servers)
- Badge marked options in reference docs
- EnvironmentOptions: define, resolve, optimizeDeps, consumer, dev, build
- DevEnvironmentOptions, BuildEnvironmentOptions: separate options per phase
- UserConfig extends EnvironmentOptions
- Backward compatibility: server.ssrLoadModule, server.moduleGraph available
- During dev: client and ssr environments always present
- During build: client always present, ssr optional (if configured)
- Custom environments: runtime providers (e.g., Cloudflare Vite plugin)
- API stable between major releases (with potential breaking changes later)
- Target users: end users (simple config), plugin authors (extended APIs), frameworks (expose differently), runtime providers (custom environments)
How do I configure multiple environments? What are the different environment types? How is Vite 6 backward compatible? How do I create custom environments?

sections.manifest:
Formalizing environments in Vite.
- Vite 5: two implicit environments (client and ssr)
- Vite 6: formal environments concept
- New API: create multiple custom environments
- Supports browser, Node server, edge server, other runtimes
- Internal refactoring with backward compatibility focus
- Smooth migration from Vite 5
How does Vite 6 formalize environments?

Closing gap between build and dev.
- SPA/MPA: client environment only (implicit)
- SSR app: two environments (client, ssr)
- Dev: server code runs in Node process (production approximation)
- Server runtimes: other JS runtimes (workerd, etc.) have different constraints
- Modern apps: browser + node server + edge server
- Vite 5 limitation: didn't represent multiple environments properly
- Vite 6: dev server runs code in multiple environments concurrently
- Source code transformed by shared Vite dev server
- Independent dev environments: HTTP server, middlewares, resolved config, plugins shared
- Each environment: configured to match production environment
- Module runner: processes modules for specific runtime
How does Vite bridge dev and build environments?

Environments configuration.
- SPA/MPA: no new APIs needed (backward compatible)
- Internally: client environment configuration
- Multiple environments: environments config option
- Explicitly configure server, edge environments
- Environment inheritance: child inherits top-level config
- Small number of top-level options apply to client only (optimizeDeps marked with badge)
- client environment: configure via top-level or environments.client
- Recommend top-level config for client (simpler)
- EnvironmentOptions interface: define, resolve, optimizeDeps, consumer, dev, build
- DevEnvironmentOptions, BuildEnvironmentOptions: dev/build specific
- optimizeDeps: dev-only but kept as top-level for backward compatibility
How do I configure multiple environments?

Custom environment instances.
- Low-level configuration APIs for runtime providers
- Runtime providers: offer environments with proper defaults
- Can spawn processes/threads for dev module execution
- Example: Cloudflare Vite plugin uses Environment API for workerd
- customEnvironment helper: create custom environment instances
- Example: ssr, edge, or custom named environments
How do I create custom environments?

Backward compatibility in Vite 6.
- Current Vite server API: not deprecated, backward compatible with Vite 5
- server.moduleGraph: mixed view of client and ssr module graphs
- Backward compatible mixed module nodes: returned from methods
- Same scheme for module nodes in handleHotUpdate
- Don't switch to Environment API yet (ecosystem adoption first)
- Framework and plugin support needed before widespread adoption
- Future deprecations: this.environment in hooks, hotUpdate hook, ModuleRunner API, Per-environment APIs, Shared plugins
- Upgrade path documented in changes section
Is Vite 6 backward compatible with Vite 5?

Target users of Environment API.
- End users: basic concepts for config
- Plugin authors: extended API in Environment API Plugins Guide
- Framework authors: Environment API Frameworks Guide for exposing environments
- Runtime providers: Environment API Runtimes Guide for custom environments
